package_info.package_versions: unknown (all available versions at time of report)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains code that establishes a reverse shell and exfiltrates data using CDN TLS termination to disguise C2 communications, enabling remote control and data theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code constructs an HTTPS request to pypi.python.org/images?guid=<b64_payload> with a custom Host header, causing the request to be routed by Fastly CDN to the attacker's C2 server, enabling exfiltration of encoded payloads and two-way C2 communication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code disguises C2 traffic as legitimate PyPI traffic by abusing CDN routing, making detection difficult and enabling covert data exfiltration and remote control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not communicate with external C2 servers or manipulate CDN routing for covert communications.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: CDN routing and custom Host headers may be used in advanced networking or CDN testing tools, but not in general-purpose Python packages.
key_indicators: Use of custom Host header targeting Fastly CDN
Exfiltration of data via HTTPS to a PyPI domain
Base64-encoded payload in URL query string

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes a reverse shell by connecting to a remote attacker's server, redirecting standard input/output/error, and spawning a shell, enabling remote command execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reverse shells are a classic method for attackers to gain remote control over a compromised system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not open remote shells or connect to arbitrary external servers for command execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Reverse shells may be used in penetration testing tools, but never in general-purpose or utility packages.
key_indicators: Duplication of file descriptors for shell

behavioral_signatures: Outbound HTTPS requests to pypi.python.org with unusual Host headers
Base64-encoded data in URL query parameters
Runtime creation of socket connections to external IPs/hosts
Spawning of shell processes (e.g., /bin/sh) from package code
file_indicators: Presence of code constructing requests to pypi.python.org with custom Host headers
Code that imports socket, subprocess, and os modules together
Unusual network-related code in __init__.py or main.py
network_indicators: HTTPS requests to pypi.python.org with Host: psec.forward.io.global.prod.fastly.net
Outbound connections to attacker-controlled IPs/domains (e.g., attacker.com:4444)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that make outbound HTTPS requests to pypi.python.org with non-standard Host headers, especially those containing base64-encoded data in the URL. Flag packages that open socket connections to external IPs or spawn shell processes at import or runtime. Review package source code for suspicious networking and process control logic.
